nodes.name: One-pot hot-injection synthesis
nodes.procedure: h-NiSe/CNTs hollow nanostructures are fabricated via a facile one-pot approach by in situ growing nickel selenide (NiSe) hollow nanocrystals (HNCs) on the self-template of carbon nanotubes (CNTs) using hot-injection route. The as-synthesized pristine NiSe nanocrystals with much larger size of ≈40 nm are obtained under the same procedure without CNTs, but they are difficult to avoid the aggregation. During the colloidal synthesis of NiSe nanocrystals in the CNTs dispersed solution, the uniformly dissolved nickel precursor is preferable to adsorb on the negatively charged CNTs with high surface free energy. Following the Ostwald ripening, the polycondensation from NiSe nuclei is thermodynamically more favorable on CNTs surface in order to minimize the surface free energies of both nanoparticles and CNTs, in which the CNTs act as the hard self-template.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform NiSe spherical nanocrystals with size of 15-20 nm are monodispersed in CNTs network with CNT diameter ≈10-15 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The uniform NiSe spherical nanocrystals with the size of 15−20 nm are monodispersed in the CNTs network (Figure 1a), where the diameter of CNT is ≈10−15 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Hollow interiors of NiSe nanocrystals with shell thickness ≈5 nm; lattice fringes correspond to (101) and (102) facets of hexagonal Sederholmite NiSe.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b exhibits the hollow interiors of NiSe nanocrystals with shell thickness of ≈5 nm. The lattice fringes in NiSe mainly correspond to the (101) and (102) facets of hexagonal Sederholmite NiSe.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM confirms hollow nature of monodispersed NiSe nanocrystals; SAED pattern shows diffraction rings for (101), (102), (110), (103) facets of NiSe and (002) facet of CNTs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image in Figure 1d and its magnified image in Figure 1e clearly show the hollow nature of monodispersed NiSe nanocrystals. The diffraction rings in SAED pattern (Figure 1f) correspond well with the (101), (102), (110), (103) facets of NiSe.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental line scan shows Ni:Se atomic ratio ≈1:1 with element intensities decreasing in the middle confirming hollow structure; mapping confirms co-existence and high dispersibility of Ni and Se.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1g presents the EDS elemental line scan crossing a nanocrystal from Figure 1e, which indicates the atomic ratio of Ni:Se is almost 1:1. Notably, their element intensities severely decrease in the middle of the distribution curve.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM confirms hollow structure of NiSe nanocrystals, high dispersibility in CNTs network, and sphere-like morphology; pristine NiSe shows larger size ≈40 nm with aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Extra SEM and TEM images (Figure S1c,d, Supporting Information) further confirm the hollow structure of NiSe nanocrystals and their high dispersibility in CNTs network.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows gradual hydroxylation/oxidation: decrease of metallic Ni peak at ≈853 eV, emergence of Ni3+ peaks at 857.2 and 875.0 eV, increased O2- at 530.1 eV, and SeOx at ≈59 eV in h-NiSe/CNTs-o.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the fresh h-NiSe/CNTs-f in Figure 3a, the h-NiSe/CNTs-s shows an obvious decrease of the XPS peak at ≈853 eV belonging to metallic Ni. The h-NiSe/CNTs-o exhibits new emerged XPS peaks at 857.2 and 875.0 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows gradual decrease of diffraction peaks for hexagonal NiSe (PDF#01-075-0610) indicating surface amorphization after hydroxylation/oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern (Figure S7, Supporting Information) shows that the gradual decrease of diffraction peaks for hexagonal NiSe (PDF#01-075-0610) over the reaction time of methanol selective oxidation.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES at Ni K-edge shows gradual increase of Ni valence; FT-EXAFS shows Ni-Se bond shortening from 2.11 Å to 2.02 Å and new Ni-O bond at ≈1.50 Å confirming surface hydroxylation/oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption edges of h-NiSe/CNTs-f, h-NiSe/CNTs-s, and h-NiSe/CNTs-o shift to the high energy... The main coordination peaks for Ni-Se in h-NiSe/CNTs-s and h-NiSe/CNTs-o gradually shift to a smaller radial distance of ≈2.05 and ≈2.02 Å.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows Ni-OOH peaks at 476 and 555 cm⁻¹ appearing at 1.42 V vs RHE; methoxyl intermediates Ni-OCH₃ with νs(CH) at ≈2845 cm⁻¹ and νas(CH) at ≈2955 cm⁻¹ during methanol oxidation at ≥1.42 V vs RHE.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In OER studies with Ni contained electrocatalysts, two Raman peaks at 476 and 555 cm⁻¹ are regarded as the Ni-O vibrations of Ni-OOH. These two characteristic Raman peaks at ≈2845 and ≈2955 cm⁻¹ become distinguishable when the working potential is no less than 1.42 V (vs RHE).
